text:
carla: Quick postmortem from the canary this morning — host-side tokenization/parse + streaming chunking produced a 3x tail latency bump on 2k-token requests. noticed after we flipped the new kv-evict heuristic. traces attached :eyes:

carla: Key observations: upstream latency normal, GPU decode stable, but host CPU on ingress spikes and grpc writev stalls. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12%.

dmitri: grabbed pprof and a flamegraph, looks like parselet::split_frame + grpc::Writev are hot. attaching a snippet: 
```
# pprof top 5
parselet::split_frame  42.1%
grpc::Writev        21.3%
kv_cache::evict      9.4%
proto::unpack        6.8%
tokenizer::normalize 5.0%
```

alice: any change to batching/kernel-selection around the canary? could be small-seq path picking wrong kernels + smaller batch fill causing more host overhead per token.

ben: yeah the kv-evict tweak we shipped reduced memory pressure but increased churn on hot keys. eviction caused more proto re-parses which seem to amplify writev fragmentation (more, smaller frames).

carla: posting actual log trace (condensed) — note repeated small writes: 
```
[2026-03-20T09:12:03.124Z] req=abcd writev bytes=512 dur=230us
[2026-03-20T09:12:03.124Z] req=abcd writev bytes=128 dur=190us
[2026-03-20T09:12:03.125Z] req=abcd kv_miss key="conv:123"
[2026-03-20T09:12:03.126Z] req=abcd parse split_frame=1.8ms proto_unwrap=0.9ms
```

infra-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-20T09:00 -> 2026-03-20T09:15 rolled out for service=host-ingress, canary_id=canary-457. Observability: latency alert triggered 2026-03-20T09:12.

dmitri: quick repro you can run locally to see the small-write pattern: 
```bash
# replay a 2k token request with short chunking
python tools/replay_request.py --file tests/2k_chunked.json --stream-chunk=128 --use-parselet
```

alice: proposal: two-pronged approach — tweak batching heuristics (raise min_batch_ms from 2ms -> 6ms to allow more accumulate) and enable proto-coalesce on ingress to reduce # of writev calls. Also add a kv-cache backoff to avoid evicting hot sessions during spikes.

ben: +1 on proto-coalesce. note: kernel selection fallback is also kicking in for short sequences; can we prefer the slim attention kernel for <512 tokens to reduce host preproc pressure? that tends to reduce host-side memcpy because the runtime avoids extra reformatting.

carla: agreed. action items: @dmitri run microbench for min_batch_ms={2,6,10} with proto-coalesce toggled, measure tail p99/p999 and kv hit-rate. @alice prototype the kv backoff feature (simple TTL bump for keys with >X hits). ben will toggle kernel preference in a canary image. I'll coordinate a 1-hour canary and capture flamegraphs.

dmitri: running now, will post numbers in ~15m. initial dry-run shows p99 drop from 420ms -> 300ms with min_batch_ms=6 and coalesce enabled. kv hit-rate recovers by ~6%.

carla: nice. lets hold full rollback until we confirm no throughput regression. file this as a postmortem note and we'll attach the repro and traces to the ticket. :thumbsup:

ben: small follow-up — watch out for increased latency for tiny requests when bumping min_batch_ms. we should A/B by request size (<=64 tokens vs >256 tokens).

carla: good call — add A/B buckets. will update the canary plan.

infra-bot: runbook update queued: add proto-coalesce toggle and batch-ms experiment to host-ingress runbook.
